title: Let athena close abandon a job whose old usage records fail reconcile
summary: Job 20261015-131540-2fsa is dispatched and interrupted, and its pre-fix invocation record fails the gate's "usage records reconcile" rule. That blocks the Abandoned close commit in `Athena::close`, and `retry` refuses dispatched jobs. I read the goal as making `athena close <job> --why` finish such a job (the operator is the audience), without weakening the gate for new records.

defaults_applied.how: New tests for the close path and the still-enforced gate; cargo test and clippy criteria.
The criteria check that closing a job with a legacy bad record succeeds.
The fix targets any job with pre-fix records, not just this one job.
The gate remains the enforcement for new records, covered by a test.
One focused change to the close path and the gate scope.
Decision and changelog entries are written for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The close commit fails because the gate re-checks the job's already-committed invocation record. I read manage.rs and reconcile.rs but did not run the failing case.
The fix goes in `close`, not `retry`, because D52 and the design say `close` is the way out for interrupted jobs.
Running `athena close` on the real job is an operator action after the change lands, and is not part of this change.
The exemption should not loosen reconciliation for newly written records.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new test builds a dispatched, interrupted job whose committed invocation record has a per-model cost sum that disagrees with its reported total (the pre-fix shape). `athena close <job> --why ...` then succeeds and writes outcome-abandoned or outcome-failed, a score record and a commit. Run `cargo test`.
A companion test shows the gate still rejects a new invocation record that fails reconciliation, and a new outcome whose totals do not match its invocations. Run `cargo test -p athena-gate`.
The closing outcome's totals are computed from the job's actual invocation records, so the outcome itself reconciles. The legacy record is left unmodified (records stay append-only).
The exemption is narrow and visible: it covers only records already committed before the close, or needs an explicit flag, and `athena close` prints which legacy records it let through.

docs/decisions.md has a new decision entry with alternatives (flag vs automatic exemption vs rewriting records), and CHANGELOG.md mentions the change, so an operator can find how to close a stuck job.
`cargo clippy` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes.

out_of_scope: Rewriting or deleting the existing invocation record in history
Changing the study or explainer work that job was doing
departures: Higher cost and time than the reference: the change touches the gate and close logic and needs a test that builds a legacy-shaped job. Lower pass chance because the exact gate scope was not confirmed.
